# Welfare and Result Tables {#sec-welfare}

## Welfare Comparison

Total expected welfare is $\E[W]=\E[U_L]+\E[U_M]$.

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{SS}}]=\E[W^{\mathrm{ML}}]
=\mu-V\kappa\nu+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{2},
$$ {#eq-ew-ss}

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=V-\mu+\frac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{2V}.
$$ {#eq-ew-lm}

::: {.proof}
By definition, $W=U_L+U_M$. For SS (and ML, which is payoff-equivalent):
$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{SS}}]
=\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]+\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]
=\left(\mu-V\kappa\nu+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}\right)+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}
=\mu-V\kappa\nu+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{2}.
$$
For LM:
$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]+\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=\frac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}+\frac{4V^2-4V\mu+\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}
=V-\mu+\frac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{2V}.
$$
:::

The sign of $\E[W^{\mathrm{SS}}]-\E[W^{\mathrm{LM}}]$ depends jointly on $V$, $\mu$, $\delta$, and distributional shape, and bears no fixed relationship to the equilibrium conditions in Section @sec-timing. To see this, note that

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{SS}}]-\E[W^{\mathrm{LM}}]
= \Delta_M - \Delta_L
= \bigl(\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]-\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]\bigr)
- \bigl(\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]-\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]\bigr).
$$

Consequently, even in the parameter region where $\Delta_L < 0$ (so that ML is the unique sequential equilibrium), if $|\Delta_M|$ is large enough relative to $|\Delta_L|$ to make $\Delta_M - \Delta_L < 0$, total welfare under LM exceeds that under SS/ML. Conversely, when $\Delta_L \ge 0$ and $\Delta_M \le 0$ (both ML and LM are equilibria), the inequality $\Delta_M - \Delta_L \le 0$ holds throughout this region, so LM weakly dominates in total welfare; yet ML is always a Nash equilibrium, so coordination on the welfare-inferior ML outcome remains possible. A potential conflict between equilibrium institution selection and welfare maximization therefore exists: individual timing incentives do not guarantee convergence to the welfare-superior regime, and this represents a notable comparative-statics observation of the model.

**Binary** ($\sigma^2=\delta^2$, $\kappa=\kappa^B$, $\nu=\nu^B$):

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{SS},B}] = \mu - V\kappa^B\nu^B + \frac{V^2(\kappa^B)^2}{2},
\qquad
\E[W^{\mathrm{LM},B}] = V - \mu + \frac{\mu^2 + \delta^2}{2V}.
$$

**Uniform** ($\sigma^2=\delta^2/3$, $\kappa=\kappa^U$, $\nu=\nu^U$):

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{SS},U}] = \mu - V\kappa^U\nu^U + \frac{V^2(\kappa^U)^2}{2},
\qquad
\E[W^{\mathrm{LM},U}] = V - \mu + \frac{3\mu^2 + \delta^2}{6V}.
$$

## Result Tables

| Object | SS (Simultaneous) | ML (Management First) | LM (Labor First) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Management information | Prior only | Prior only | Observes $x_L$ and infers type |
| Equilibrium type | Bayesian Nash | Same as SS | Unique separating PBE |
| $x_M$ | $\dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | $\dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | $\dfrac{v(2V-v)}{4V}$ |
| $x_L$ | $\dfrac{V\kappa}{2}\sqrt{v} - \dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | Same as SS | $\dfrac{v^2}{4V}$ |
| $U_L$ | $\left(\sqrt{v}-\dfrac{V\kappa}{2}\right)^{\!2}$ | Same as SS | $\dfrac{v^2}{4V}$ |
| $U_M$ | $\dfrac{V^2\kappa}{2\sqrt{v}} - \dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | Same as SS | $\dfrac{(2V-v)^2}{4V}$ |
| $\E[U_L]$ | $\mu - V\kappa\nu + \dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | Same as SS | $\dfrac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}$ |
| $\E[U_M]$ | $\dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | $\dfrac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}$ | $\dfrac{4V^2-4V\mu+\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}$ |

: Equilibrium summary in the generalized model {#tbl-summary-general}

where $\kappa=\E[V_L^{-1/2}]$, $\nu=\E[V_L^{1/2}]$, and $\sigma^2=\Var(V_L)$.

| Moment / Structure | Binary | Uniform |
|---|---|---|
| $\sigma^2$ | $\delta^2$ | $\delta^2/3$ |
| $\kappa$ | $\dfrac{1}{2u_\ell}+\dfrac{1}{2u_H}$ | $\dfrac{u_H-u_\ell}{\delta}$ |
| $\nu$ | $\dfrac{u_\ell+u_H}{2}$ | $\dfrac{u_H^3-u_\ell^3}{3\delta}$ |
